evidence.description: The task expressly withholds the premise needed for this issue class: it does not establish that k1 or k2 identifies a source item, so a repeated k1 code cannot be shown to be a repeated entry of the same independent unit.
evidence.observed_value: codes declared opaque; unit identity not established

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items measured by columns `a` and `b`. Treat `k1` and `k2` as opaque codes; `tag` is an opaque annotation. This task does not establish whether either code identifies a source item within either collection. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the items represented in that row.

evidence.description: The workflow applies an independent-samples t-test to all row values, which would only instantiate the issue class if repeated unit identity were established, which it is not.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict by treating the repeated k1 codes (each of u01–u06 appearing twice, entered into ttest_ind with df=22 confirming all 24 values were used) as demonstrating repeated unit entry. This fails because the governing task explicitly states it does not establish whether either code identifies a source item, so the visible files cannot demonstrate that any independent unit entered the procedure more than once; code repetition alone does not demonstrate unit repetition. The task's declaration is definitional rather than ambiguous, so no blocking question remains.
